title: feat: optionally distribute replicas across architectures
description:
Adds an optional topologySpreadConstraints field to Connect, Workbench,
and Package Manager, so a Site can guarantee its product replicas split
across topology domains — e.g. one amd64 and one arm64 replica in a
multi-arch cluster — instead of relying only on the operator's existing
soft, hostname-keyed anti-affinity.

An omitted labelSelector on a constraint is auto-filled to the
component's own pod labels, since Kubernetes otherwise treats a nil
selector as matching zero pods, silently turning the constraint into a
no-op. An explicit caller-supplied selector is never overridden.

- Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/team-operator/issues/152

title: feat(chronicle): make chronicle-server resources configurable
description:
## What

Adds an optional `resources` field to `ChronicleSpec` (surfaced through the
Site-level `InternalChronicleSpec`) that sets the `chronicle-server`
container's resource requests and limits.

- **Unset (default):** requests `cpu=100m` / `memory=1Gi`, limit `memory=4Gi`,
  no CPU limit.
- **Set:** the provided `ResourceRequirements` replaces the defaults entirely.

## Why

`chronicle-server` previously ran with empty requests and **no limits**. On a
high-ingest workload its refinement/aggregation memory can grow unbounded,
driving a **node-level OOM** that evicts chronicle and its neighbors, then
recurs on the next node. With `request=0` it is also the kubelet's first
eviction victim.

Giving the container a default memory limit converts a runaway into a
**contained cgroup OOMKill of chronicle alone** instead of a node-wide OOM.
The per-site override exists so deployments that legitimately need more
headroom can raise the ceiling rather than crashloop.

## Changes

- `api/core/v1beta1`: new `Resources *corev1.ResourceRequirements` on
  `ChronicleSpec` and `InternalChronicleSpec` (+ generated deepcopy).
- `client-go/applyconfiguration`: regenerated apply configs (`WithResources`).
- `internal/controller/core/chronicle_controller.go`: apply
  `Spec.Resources` to the container, falling back to a package-level default.
- `internal/controller/core/site_controller_chronicle.go`: thread
  `Spec.Chronicle.Resources` into the built `Chronicle`.
- CRDs regenerated in all three locations (`config/crd`, `dist/chart`,
  `internal/crdapply`).
- Tests: default-resources and override-resources cases for the reconciler.

## Testing

- [x] `make manifests generate` leaves the tree clean
- [x] `make test`
- [ ] Deployed via adhoc image to a test cluster; verified default + override
      land on the StatefulSet pod spec

title: feat: allow Connect content pods to run on tainted session nodes
description:
# Description

Extends the existing Workbench session toleration/placement capability to Posit Connect content pods. Connect content (off-host execution) pods can now be both permitted onto (via tolerations) and directed to (via a node selector) tainted Karpenter session nodes, exactly mirroring how Workbench session pods already work.

Two new optional fields are added to the Connect site spec:

- `contentTolerations` — tolerations applied only to Connect content (session) pods, not the Connect server.
- `contentNodeSelector` — a node selector applied only to Connect content (session) pods, not the Connect server.

This directly parallels the existing Workbench `sessionTolerations` mechanism, but for Connect's content pods.

## Code Flow

- `api/core/v1beta1/site_types.go`: adds `ContentTolerations` and `ContentNodeSelector` to `InternalConnectSpec`.
- `internal/controller/core/site_controller_connect.go`: wires those fields into the Connect `SessionConfig.Pod` (`product.PodConfig`) as `Tolerations` and `NodeSelector`, mirroring `site_controller_workbench.go` which sets session `Tolerations`/`NodeSelector` for Workbench session pods.
- No template changes are needed: `api/templates/*/job.tpl` already renders `pod.tolerations` and `pod.nodeSelector`.
- Generated CRDs, deepcopy, client-go applyconfig, and the Helm chart CRD were regenerated via `just mgenerate` / the Helm chart generation hook.

title: fix: prevent YAML line-wrap in Workbench job launcher template
description:
## Summary

Replicates the fix from [rstudio/helm#795](https://github.com/rstudio/helm/pull/795) into team-operator's vendored Workbench launcher job template.

Go's `yaml.Marshal` wraps strings at 80 characters by default. In `job.tpl`, the `name` annotation (session name + IDs + username + project name) and the `service_ports` annotation (JSON port mappings) can exceed 80 chars. When they wrap, the continuation line lands at the wrong indentation, producing invalid YAML that Kubernetes rejects with a `400 Bad Request` — breaking Workbench session launch for users with long project names or many service ports.

## Fix

Add the `| indent 8 | trimPrefix (repeat 8 " ")` guard to the `name` and `service_ports` lines, matching the pattern already used by the adjacent `stdin` and `user_metadata` annotations:

```diff
-        name: {{ toYaml .Job.name }}
-        service_ports: {{ toYaml .Job.servicePortsJson }}
+        name: {{ toYaml .Job.name | indent 8 | trimPrefix (repeat 8 " ") }}
+        service_ports: {{ toYaml .Job.servicePortsJson | indent 8 | trimPrefix (repeat 8 " ") }}
```

Applied to `api/templates/2.5.0/job.tpl` — the only version embedded and used by the operator (`//go:embed 2.5.0/job.tpl`, consumed by workbench.go and connect.go). The `2.4.0`/`2.3.1` directories are unreferenced historical copies and are intentionally left untouched.

## Testing

- [ ] Deploy adhoc image to a test cluster and launch a Workbench session with a long project name / multiple service ports; confirm the launcher job applies cleanly.

There are currently no template-rendering tests for `job.tpl` in this repo. A follow-up unit test that renders the template with a long `name`/`servicePortsJson` and asserts the output parses as valid YAML would guard against regression (out of scope here).

title: feat: add configurable resource requests/limits for Connect, Workbench, and Package Manager
description:
# Description

Connect and Workbench server pods shipped as **BestEffort** QoS (empty `ResourceRequirements`). On a shared node, a co-located CPU-saturating workload (e.g. a Workbench launched job pinning the node at 100% CPU) can starve the server of CPU shares — in production this drove a Connect replica into CrashLoopBackOff (its launcher `/v1/status` health-check timed out, so Connect self-terminated).

This adds a configurable `resources` field to the **Connect**, **Workbench**, and **Package Manager** server specs, with **fleet-wide default requests** so these pods get a guaranteed CPU/memory floor (**Burstable** QoS) under contention.

Defaults are **requests-only** for all three products (no hard limits → no memory-OOMKill ceiling on the server pods), sourced from the published Posit Helm charts. Package Manager previously carried hard-coded requests **and** limits; this change drops its limits for **parity** with Connect/Workbench and to align with the upstream chart, which ships limits disabled by default (its requests are unchanged). Setting `resources` in `site.yaml` replaces the product default entirely (standard `ResourceRequirements` semantics, no per-field merge).

### Default values and sources (Posit Helm charts — https://docs.posit.co/helm/)

| Product | Default requests | Default limits | Chart source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connect | cpu `100m`, mem `1Gi` | none | [`rstudio-connect` values.yaml](https://github.com/rstudio/helm/blob/main/charts/rstudio-connect/values.yaml) |
| Workbench | cpu `100m`, mem `2Gi` | none | [`rstudio-workbench` values.yaml](https://github.com/rstudio/helm/blob/main/charts/rstudio-workbench/values.yaml) |
| Package Manager | cpu `100m`, mem `2Gi`, eph `500Mi` | none *(previously cpu `2000m` / mem `4Gi` / eph `2Gi` — removed for parity)* | [`rstudio-pm` values.yaml](https://github.com/rstudio/helm/blob/main/charts/rstudio-pm/values.yaml) |

The Helm charts ship these `resources` blocks **disabled by default**; we adopt their request values as the operator default while leaving limits off for all three products, matching the charts' "limits disabled" stance. (Flightdeck keeps its existing inline limits — it's an internal component, out of scope for this change.)

## Code Flow

The Site CR fans out to per-product CRs, so the field is plumbed through both layers:

```
site.yaml spec.<product>.resources
  → Internal<Product>Spec            (api/core/v1beta1/site_types.go)
  → copied in site_controller_<product>.go (reconcile<Product>)
  → <Product>Spec.Resources          (api/core/v1beta1/<product>_types.go)
  → read by the pod builder
```

Each pod builder resolves the effective resources with `utilptr.Deref(<product>.Spec.Resources, <product>DefaultResources)` (`k8s.io/utils/ptr`) — the site-provided override when set, otherwise a package-level default var (`connectDefaultResources` / `workbenchDefaultResources` / `packageManagerDefaultResources`). PTD applies `site.yaml` to the Site CR verbatim (untyped passthrough), so no PTD-side code change is needed — only a `team_operator_chart_version` bump once this releases.

## Category of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

**Fleet-wide impact on upgrade:**
- **Connect / Workbench**: transition BestEffort → Burstable (default requests applied). CPU request is trivial (`100m`); memory requests reserve capacity the servers already use.
- **Package Manager**: stays Burstable, requests unchanged, but its previously hard-coded CPU/memory/ephemeral **limits are removed** — notably its prior 4Gi memory OOMKill ceiling is lifted.
- No product has a default memory *limit*, so no new OOMKill behavior is introduced anywhere. Any site can still set explicit `resources` (incl. limits) in `site.yaml` to override.

Validated end-to-end on a dev cluster via an adhoc image: CRD accepted the new field (operator self-applies its embedded CRDs at startup), defaults produced the expected Burstable pods, and a `site.yaml` override propagated Site → product CR → pod.

## Checklist

- [x] I have run the tests and all pass — `make go-test` is green (all 6 per-product resource tests + full `controller/core` package). Note: bare `just test` does not provision envtest assets (`KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS`), so use `make go-test` / `just mtest`.
- [x] I have reviewed my own diff

title: fix: correct load-balancer XDG_CONFIG_DIRS path so Workbench finds config
description:
## Description

Fixes the Workbench HA load-balancer config never being read, which caused nodes to fall back to pod hostnames (unresolvable in cluster DNS) and fail to reach each other.

### Root cause

`XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` entries are *base* directories — Workbench appends `rstudio/<filename>` to each when resolving config files. The load-balancer init container writes its config to `/mnt/load-balancer/rstudio/load-balancer`, so the XDG entry must be `/mnt/load-balancer`.

The entry was `/mnt/load-balancer/rstudio`, so Workbench looked for `/mnt/load-balancer/rstudio/rstudio/load-balancer`, which never exists. On startup Workbench logged:

```
No load balancing configuration 'load-balancer' found in XDG_CONFIG_DIRS, expected in an 'rstudio' folder in one of '...:/mnt/load-balancer/rstudio'
Load balancer default for missing www-host-name using system hostname: <pod-name>:8787
```

Because `www-host-name` defaulted to the pod name (not the pod IP from the load-balancer file), HA nodes tried to reach each other by pod hostname, which is not resolvable via cluster DNS:

```
ERROR asio.netdb error 1 (Host not found (authoritative)) [host: <pod-name>:8787, uri: /load-balancer/distributed_events ...]
```

This degraded session routing in multi-replica Workbench deployments (failed distributed events, white screens on session creation).

### Fix

Set the XDG entry to `/mnt/load-balancer` in both locations (`InitializeNonRootSupervisorConfig` and `CreateVolumeFactory`), and add a comment explaining the base-dir semantics to prevent regression. The previous value was introduced during review of #129, which had originally used the correct path.

### Verification

Reproduced on a staging cluster: a freshly rolled Workbench pod logged the "No load balancing configuration found" message and defaulted `www-host-name` to the pod name. With the corrected path, Workbench reads the file and uses the pod IP.

## Category of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass (`make go-test`, exit 0)

title: feat: add envVars field for Workbench, Connect, and Package Manager
description:
## Summary

Adds a new `envVars` field (`[]corev1.EnvVar`) to the **Workbench**, **Connect**, and **Package Manager** product specs (both the standalone product CRs and the Site-embedded specs). Unlike the existing `addEnv` (`map[string]string`, literals only), `envVars` supports the standard Kubernetes `EnvVar` structure including `valueFrom` (e.g. `secretKeyRef`), so secrets can be injected the Kubernetes-native way.

The existing `addEnv` field is **deprecated** in favor of `envVars` but continues to work. `envVars` is appended last when assembling the container `Env`, so it takes precedence on a name conflict.

Scope is intentionally limited to the three "product itself" pods. Workbench sessions already have `sessionEnvVars`; Connect content and Chronicle are not included.

## Usage

```yaml
apiVersion: core.posit.team/v1beta1
kind: Site
spec:
  packageManager:
    envVars:
      - name: PM_API_KEY
        valueFrom:
          secretKeyRef:
            name: my-secret
            key: api-key
```

The same `envVars` field is available under `spec.connect` and `spec.workbench`.

## Changes

- API types: `envVars` added to Connect/Workbench/PackageManager specs and their Site-embedded internal specs; `addEnv` marked deprecated.
- Controllers: Site → product copy of `envVars`; `envVars` appended to the container `Env` render path for all three products.
- Regenerated: deepcopy, CRD bases (+ embedded copies), Helm chart CRDs, client-go applyconfiguration, openapi.
- Docs: `docs/api-reference.md` updated with `envVars` rows and `addEnv` deprecation notes.

## Testing

- `TestSiteReconciler_EnvVars` — verifies Site → product CR propagation (including a `secretKeyRef` entry) for all three products.
- `TestPackageManagerReconciler_EnvVars` — verifies both a plain var and a `secretKeyRef` var reach the rendered Package Manager container `Env`.
- `make manifests generate-all` idempotent, `make verify-crds`, `make fmt vet build`, and `make test` all pass.

title: feat: pin Positron Pro version via positronConfig.version
description:
## Summary

- Adds `positronConfig.version` to `Site.Spec.Workbench.PositronSettings` so operators can pin a non-default Positron Pro version for Workbench sessions.
- When set, the controller writes three new rserver.conf keys (`launcher-positron-init-container-enabled`, `-image-name`, `-image-tag`) that Workbench's Launcher reads to attach the `posit/workbench-positron-init:<version>` init container to every session pod (delivers the pinned binary to a shared volume).
- Auto-derives `positron.conf` `exe` to `/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/positron-server/<version>/bin/positron-server` (the path the init container delivers to). An explicit user-supplied `Exe` always wins.
- Mirrors the upstream Posit Workbench Helm chart's `components.positron.version` UX in one knob; team-operator constructs pod specs/rserver.conf directly and doesn't consume the chart, so the equivalent wiring is added here.

## Example

```yaml
spec:
  workbench:
    positronConfig:
      version: "2026.04.0-269"
```

## Notes

- Image name is hardcoded to `posit/workbench-positron-init` (matches the upstream chart default). Customers needing a mirrored registry can route around it via `AdditionalConfigs` until a dedicated knob is justified.
- Server-pod init container (the chart adds one for the Admin UI's version browser) is intentionally out of scope — sessions work without it. Can be added as a follow-up if needed.
- No validation/regex on the version string — Workbench rejects an invalid tag at session-start time.

## Test plan

- [x] `just mgenerate` — CRDs and client-go applyconfig regenerated; diff confined to the three new fields

The Workbench probe is unauthenticated. Any override must point to an endpoint that does not require auth and returns 2xx-3xx, otherwise the pod will never become ready. title: fix: add /mnt/load-balancer to XDG_CONFIG_DIRS so Workbench reads load-balancer config
description:
## Description

The init container writes `/mnt/load-balancer/rstudio/load-balancer` with load-balancer settings (`delete-node-on-exit=1`, `www-host-name=<pod-ip>`). The volume is mounted at `/mnt/load-balancer` on the main Workbench container, but `/mnt/load-balancer` was absent from `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS`, so Workbench never discovered or read the file.

## Code Flow

`XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` is set in two places in `api/core/v1beta1/workbench_types.go`:

1. `InitializeNonRootSupervisorConfig` (~line 497) — the supervisord `Environment:` string used in NonRoot mode
2. `CreateVolumeFactory` (~line 696) — the `Env` var on the `"config-volume"` volume definition for the main pod

Both now include `/mnt/load-balancer` as the final path component, matching where the init container writes the config file.

title: fix: prevent status-patch reconcile storm in Site and child controllers
description:
## Summary

- The status improvement in commit eb3f7b0 introduced `SetProgressing(true)` at the start of every reconcile for Site and all child controllers, followed by `SetProgressing(false)` at the end. This flips `LastTransitionTime` on every cycle, making every status patch non-empty.
- Without a generation predicate on `For()`, those status patches fire watch events that re-enqueue the reconciler — a self-perpetuating loop.
- On a staging cluster this drove the Site controller to ~180 reconciles/second across all sites, causing elevated network packet rates on the controller node.
- `PostgresDatabaseReconciler` already had `GenerationChangedPredicate` applied correctly; this PR applies the same fix to the remaining six controllers.

Added `builder.WithPredicates(predicate.GenerationChangedPredicate{})` to the `For()` call in `SetupWithManager` for: `SiteReconciler`, `ConnectReconciler`, `WorkbenchReconciler`, `PackageManagerReconciler`, `ChronicleReconciler`, `FlightdeckReconciler`.

`Owns()` watches are intentionally left without the predicate so child status changes continue to propagate up to `aggregateChildStatus`.

title: feat: add session label controller for Workbench session pods
description:
# Description

Adds a `SessionGroupLabelReconciler` that watches Workbench session pods and injects numbered labels derived from values extracted from a configurable pod field — e.g. `user-group-1: some_value`, `user-group-2: another_value`. Labels can be consumed by any downstream tooling that reads pod metadata.

Replaces functionality for: https://github.com/posit-dev/team-operator/pull/113
Intends to be more lightweight and supportable.

## How it works

The controller reads a configurable field from each session pod, applies a regex to find matching entries, sanitizes them to valid Kubernetes label values, and patches the pod with numbered labels (up to 30). A `posit.co/session-group-labels-injected: "true"` marker prevents reprocessing.

Configuration is per-site via a new `sessionLabels` field on the Workbench CRD. Adding it to `site.yaml` enables the feature for that site; omitting it disables it. PTD automatically enables the controller via Helm when any site has the block configured — no manual flag needed.

## Enabling

```yaml
# site.yaml
spec:
  workbench:
    sessionLabels:
      sourceField: "spec.containers[0].args"  # dot-path into pod spec; supports array index notation
      sourceKey: "--container-user-groups"     # flag name (args) or map key (annotations/labels)
      searchRegex: "_entra_[^ ,]+"            # only matching comma-separated entries become labels
      trimPrefix: "_"                          # stripped from the start of each matched value
```

All fields are optional — defaults cover the standard Workbench + Entra ID setup.

## Reprocessing existing pods

By default, already-processed pods are skipped (the marker label prevents re-reconciliation). To force re-labeling of existing session pods — e.g. after changing `searchRegex` or `trimPrefix` — set `reprocess: true`:

```yaml
sessionLabels:
  reprocess: true   # re-labels all existing session pods for this site immediately
```

When `reprocess: true` is set on a Workbench CR, the controller re-enqueues all existing session pods for that site immediately. Previously written group labels are cleared before the new set is applied, so stale labels from the old config are removed. Set back to `false` (or omit it) once done — it defaults to `false` and has no effect otherwise.

## Config flow

```
site.yaml workbench.sessionLabels
  → PTD detects block, sets sessionGroupLabels.enable=true in Helm
  → SiteReconciler propagates to Workbench CR
  → SessionGroupLabelReconciler reads config at reconcile time
  → Pod labels: user-group-1: <matched_value_1>
                user-group-2: <matched_value_2>
```

title: fix: prevent non-deterministic reconcile loops
description:
# Description

Fix a tight reconcile feedback loop that caused the operator pod to crash will infinitely spawning new Workbench instances and shutting down old. Both Workbench CRs on a test cluster had runaway generation counts (`workbench1`: 129,645, `workbench2`: 77,959) while Connect and Package Manager CRs were stable at single digits. Multiple independent non-determinism bugs were producing spurious spec diffs on every reconcile due to Go's non-deterministic map iteration.

### Fix 1: Sort resource profile keys (`site_controller_workbench.go`)

`getResourceProfileKeys()` iterated a map without sorting, so the `ResourceProfiles` slice in the Workbench spec had a random order on each Site reconcile. `equality.Semantic.DeepEqual` is order-sensitive for slices, so most reconciles saw a diff and wrote the Workbench spec. This incremented the generation, which triggered the Workbench controller (via `ObservedGeneration` + `Owns()` watch), which patched status, which re-triggered the Site controller — a tight loop.

### Fix 2: Sort map keys in secret generation (`secret.go`)

`mapToJmesPath()` and `generateSecretObjects()` iterated maps without sorting, producing non-deterministic YAML and `SecretObjects` ordering. This caused `CreateOrUpdateResource` to rewrite the `SecretProviderClass` on every Workbench reconcile, adding unnecessary API write traffic.

Both functions now sort keys before iterating, matching the existing pattern in `ComputeSha256` and `SecretVolumeFactory.EnvVars()`.

### Fix 3: Sort volume mounts deterministically (`volumes.go`)

`VolumeFactory.VolumeMounts()` sorted by volume name only, but multiple mounts can share the same name (e.g. a configmap mounted at different subpaths). The sort was unstable for same-name mounts, so `positron.conf` and `workbench_nss.conf` swapped positions on each reconcile, causing the Deployment spec to differ every time. With `Owns(&Deployment{})`, this created a secondary feedback loop of continuous Deployment updates and pod rollouts. Fixed by adding `MountPath` as a tiebreaker.

### Fix 4: Use `Data` instead of `StringData` for workbench config Secret (`workbench.go`)

`StringData` is write-only in the Kubernetes API: the server converts it to `Data` on create and always returns `StringData` as `nil` on read. `CreateOrUpdate` always saw a diff (pre-mutation `StringData=nil` vs post-mutation `StringData` set), rewriting the Secret on every reconcile. Fixed by using `secret.Data` with `[]byte` values directly.

### Fix 5: Skip subdir-provisioning Job when one already completed (`subdir.go`)

`provisionSubDirectoryCreator()` generated a new Job name with a random suffix (`provisionerName + "-" + RandStringBytes(6)`) on every reconcile. Because the name was always unique, `CreateOrUpdateResource` created a brand-new Job each time rather than finding an existing one — spawning an endless stream of subdir-provisioning pods. The original code even had a TODO acknowledging this: `// TODO: some way to ensure that we do not spawn _too many_ jobs...?`

Fixed by listing existing Jobs matching the Site's labels before creating a new one. If any Job whose name starts with the provisioner prefix has a `Complete` condition, the reconciler skips Job creation entirely. The Job is idempotent (`mkdir -p`), so re-running it is harmless but wasteful and generates a ton of pods.

### Why this became a crash when the code has existed for a while

Both non-determinism bugs are pre-existing, but they were largely dormant before #94 (`feat: improve status on team operator resources`). PR 94 added `Owns(&Workbench{})` to the Site controller and `ObservedGeneration` tracking to the Workbench controller. These are correct patterns, but together they closed a feedback loop that the non-determinism needed to self-sustain:

- **Before #94:** Spurious Workbench spec writes still happened, but the Site controller didn't watch Workbench objects. The loop only ran when something else independently triggered a Site reconcile (e.g., periodic resync). Slow burn.
- **After #94:** Spec write → generation++ → Workbench reconcile patches `ObservedGeneration` → status change fires `Owns` watch → Site re-enqueued → builds `ResourceProfiles` in new random order → spec write → repeat at ~3/sec.

title: feat: add optional SCIM provisioning support for Workbench
description:
# Description

Adds opt-in SCIM user provisioning for Workbench, allowing an external IdP (e.g. Okta, Entra ID) to manage users and groups via the Workbench SCIM v2 API without requiring first-login.

**API** — new `scim` block on `Site.spec.workbench`:

```yaml
spec:
  workbench:
    scim:
      enabled: true
      tokenSecretName: my-secret  # optional — omit to auto-generate
```

**Operator behaviour when `scim.enabled: true`:**
- Generates a cryptographically random bearer token (32 bytes, base64url) and stores it in a managed Secret named `<site-name>-workbench-scim-token` in `posit-team`. The token is never rotated automatically; deleting the Secret triggers regeneration on the next reconcile.
- Alternatively, point `tokenSecretName` at a pre-existing Secret with a `token` key (BYO mode). The operator uses it as-is and does not manage its lifecycle.
- Mounts the token into the Workbench pod at `/etc/rstudio/scim-token` via a Secret volume.
- Sets `WORKBENCH_USER_SERVICE_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH=/etc/rstudio/scim-token` on the Workbench container so Workbench can locate the token at startup.

With this in place, Workbench enables the `https://<workbench-hostname>/scim/v2/Users` endpoint for IDPs to call. I was able to test with direct curl calls to this endpoint, simulating what an IDP would do, creating users, editing their attributes, creating groups, and cleaning it all up.

**Retrieve the token to configure your IdP:**
```bash
kubectl get secret <site-name>-workbench-scim-token \
  -n posit-team -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d
```

Configure your IdP SCIM endpoint as `https://<workbench-hostname>/scim/v2` with Bearer token auth.

### Code Flow

| `api/core/v1beta1/site_types.go` | `WorkbenchSCIMConfig` struct; `SCIM` field on `InternalWorkbenchSpec` |

title: feat: add Connect/Workbench PPM authenticated repos via Identity Federation
description:
## Description

Enable Connect and Workbench to authenticate against PPM using Kubernetes Identity Federation (RFC 8693 token exchange). When `authenticatedRepos: true` is set on a product spec, the operator automatically injects init container + sidecar pods that exchange K8s projected service account tokens for PPM API tokens, writing netrc/curlrc files for Python and R package installation.

## Issue

- PTDC-223: Configure Connect to automatically use PPM authenticated repos
- PTDC-222: Configure Workbench to automatically use PPM authenticated repos

## Dependencies

- Depends on #112 (PPM OIDC/SSO web UI configuration) merging first. Once merged, this PR should be rebased onto main to show only the auth repos diff.

## Code Flow

### Authentication Flow
```
K8s Projected SA Token → Init Container → PPM /__api__/token (RFC 8693) → PPM API Token
                                                                                │
                                                                        Written to netrc + curlrc
                                                                                │
                         Connect/Workbench ← reads netrc/curlrc ←───────────────┘
                         (R: CURL_HOME, Python: NETRC env var)

Sidecar refreshes the token on a timer (default 50min for 60min token lifetime).
```

### Key Components

1. **PPM Identity Federation Config** (`package_manager_config.go`): `PackageManagerIdentityFederationConfig` struct with full field coverage. Extended `GenerateGcfg()` to emit named `[IdentityFederation "connect"]` sections.

2. **Token Exchange Helpers** (`ppm_auth.go`): Shared functions for init container, sidecar container, volumes, volume mounts, and env vars. Shell script (mounted from ConfigMap) uses wget + sed (BusyBox built-ins in alpine:3) for zero-dependency operation.

3. **Product Integration** (`connect.go`, `workbench.go`): When `AuthenticatedRepos=true`, adds projected SA token volume, shared emptyDir, script ConfigMap volume, init container, sidecar container, NETRC + CURL_HOME env vars.

4. **Site Controller** (`site_controller.go`): Creates `{site}-ppm-auth-script` ConfigMap when any product has authenticated repos enabled. Auto-configures Identity Federation entries on PPM based on product flags.

description:
## Description

Enable OIDC authentication for the Package Manager web UI. Adds first-class OIDC configuration types and full typed coverage of all PPM authentication config fields from the [PPM configuration reference](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/appendix/configuration.html#authentication).

When `auth.type: oidc` is set on the Site's `packageManager` spec, the operator automatically configures the `[OpenIDConnect]` and `[Authentication]` gcfg sections and mounts the OIDC client secret from the vault.

## Issue

- PTDC-224: Configure SSO (OIDC) for Package Manager web UI

## Follow-up

Connect/Workbench authenticated repos via Identity Federation is in #114.

## Code Flow

### Key Components

1. **PPM Authentication Config Types** (`package_manager_config.go`): New `PackageManagerAuthenticationConfig` and `PackageManagerOIDCConfig` structs with full field coverage from the PPM configuration reference. Extended `GenerateGcfg()` to emit `[Authentication]` and `[OpenIDConnect]` sections.

2. **OIDC Client Secret Mount** (`packagemanager_types.go`): Mounts the OIDC client secret at `/etc/rstudio-pm/oidc-client-secret` via SecretProviderClass (AWS) or K8s Secret volume (K8s).

3. **Site Controller Propagation** (`site_controller_package_manager.go`): Propagates OIDC config from Site spec to PackageManager, setting `ClientSecretFile`, `Issuer`, `ClientId`, `RequireLogin`, and `Scope`.

4. **SecretProviderClass** (`package_manager.go`): Adds OIDC client secret to the SecretProviderClass when `OIDCClientSecretKey` is configured.

### SiteSpec Example
```yaml
spec:
  packageManager:
    auth:
      type: oidc
      clientId: "ppm-client-id"
      issuer: "https://login.example.com"
    oidcClientSecretKey: "ppm-oidc-client-secret"
```

## Testing

Tested end-to-end on `ganso01-staging` (main site) with adhoc image `adhoc-ppm-auth-repos-v1.16.1-15-gedc6aaa`.

### Setup
- **Keycloak**: Created `posit` realm with `ppm` client (confidential, authorization code grant type)
- **OIDC client secret**: Stored in AWS Secrets Manager, mounted to PPM at `/etc/rstudio-pm/oidc-client-secret`

### Results

| Test | Status |
|------|--------|
| PPM gcfg renders `[OpenIDConnect]` section with `ClientSecretFile` | ✅ |
| PPM gcfg renders `[Authentication]` section | ✅ |
| PPM OIDC web login redirects to Keycloak (`/__login__` → 302 to Keycloak auth endpoint) | ✅ |
| OIDC client secret mounted at `/etc/rstudio-pm/oidc-client-secret` | ✅ |

### Note on repo authentication
PPM's OIDC redirect only activates when repos are configured as "Authenticated". The `[OpenIDConnect]` section enables the OIDC provider, but individual repos must be marked as authenticated (via `rspm edit repo --name=<repo> --authenticated` or creating repos with `--authenticated` flag). title: feat: operator applies own CRDs at startup to ensure schema matches binary
description:
## Why

When testing PR #93 via `adhoc_team_operator_image`, only the container image
was swapped — not the Helm chart. The cluster's CRDs stayed at v1.11.0 and
rejected the new `connect.enabled` field introduced in that PR. The same issue
can occur whenever an operator image is deployed without a corresponding Helm
chart upgrade (adhoc testing, emergency image patches, etc.).

## What

The operator now applies its own CRDs at startup using Kubernetes server-side
apply (SSA), ensuring the CRD schema always matches the running binary.

- New `internal/crdapply` package with `//go:embed` for all 7 CRD manifests
- `ApplyCRDs` applies them via SSA with field manager `"team-operator"` — idempotent, only patches when schema differs
- New `--manage-crds` flag (default `true`) to opt out if you manage CRDs externally
- `make copy-crds` keeps embedded files in sync with generated CRDs; hooked into `make build`
- RBAC updated to allow `get/create/patch/update` on `customresourcedefinitions`
- `dist/chart/values.yaml` includes `--manage-crds=true` in default args

## Does this conflict with `helm upgrade`?

No. A few cases:

**Normal upgrade (chart + image updated together):** Both Helm (`"helm"` field
manager) and the operator (`"team-operator"`) apply identical content — SSA
makes this a no-op regardless of order. Field ownership bounces between
managers silently but causes no semantic change.

**Adhoc image (operator newer than chart):** No Helm upgrade is happening, so
the operator is the only writer. No conflict.

**Helm upgrade with mismatched older chart:** Helm would overwrite the
operator-applied schema for that upgrade. The operator doesn't re-watch CRDs
post-startup, so the old schema would persist until the next pod restart. This
is a deliberately misconfigured state and expected behavior.

**GitOps users (Flux/ArgoCD):** Pass `--manage-crds=false` or set
`controllerManager.container.args` in `values.yaml` to opt out entirely.

## Testing

- Unit test in `internal/crdapply/` verifies all 7 CRDs embed and parse correctly
- `go build ./...` compiles cleanly
- Manual verification: deploy with `adhoc_team_operator_image`, confirm new fields accepted without manual CRD patching

## Summary

Reworks the Connect enable/disable API introduced in #80. The original implementation treated `enabled: false` as a fully destructive operation. This PR splits that into two explicit fields:

- `enabled: false` — non-destructive suspend: removes the Deployment, Service, and Ingress but preserves the PVC, database, and secrets. Re-enabling picks up all existing data without data loss.
- `teardown: true` — explicit destructive teardown (only takes effect when `enabled: false`): deletes the Connect CR, triggering the finalizer that destroys all resources including the database.

Adds a `Suspended` field to `ConnectSpec` (internal, set by the Site controller) to signal the Connect reconciler to remove serving resources without touching data.

## Use cases

- Customer doesn't have a Connect license yet → deploy site with `enabled: false`, enable later when they purchase
- Customer wants to stop using Connect temporarily → `enabled: false` preserves data
- Customer permanently decommissioning Connect → `enabled: false` + `teardown: true`

title: fix: remove deprecated DefaultContentListView
description:
found this warning in a connect instance that's 2025.12:

```
Warning: The setting Server.DefaultContentListView is deprecated and will be removed in an upcoming release. This setting no longer has any effect and will be removed in a future release.
```

> Server.DefaultContentListView is explicitly marked as deprecated and “will be removed in an upcoming release.” [[DefaultContentListView](https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/appendix/configuration/index.html#Server.DefaultContentListView)]

> The newer releases of Posit Connect have moved to a new tabbed UI for the content list (My Work / All, with searching and filtering) and no longer rely on the old “compact vs expanded” default view setting. [[Connect 2025.09.0](https://docs.posit.co/connect/news/index.html#posit-connect-2025.09.0)]

> From the available documentation:

> There is no direct replacement configuration option documented for Server.DefaultContentListView.
The docs only say it is deprecated and will be removed; they do not specify a new setting you should switch to.
So:

> You should plan to remove Server.DefaultContentListView from your configuration, since it may stop working in a future release.
> There is nothing you need to replace it with; users can still choose how they view content via the UI, but there is no new admin-level default-view setting documented.
> If you need behavior similar to what you previously enforced with DefaultContentListView, the knowledge sources do not describe any supported replacement mechanism.

## Problem
The operator's manager fails to sync informer caches when Site CRDs don't exist, causing crashes with:
```
Could not wait for Cache to sync {"controller": "ptdconfig"}
failed to get informer from cache {"error": "Timeout: failed waiting for *unstructured.Unstructured Informer to sync"}
problem running manager {"error": "failed to wait for site caches to sync kind source: *v1.Flightdeck: timed out waiting for cache to be synced"}
```

## Solution
1. Added `isCRDPresent()` helper function to check if CRDs exist before setting up controllers
2. Site and Flightdeck controllers are now only registered if their respective CRDs exist
3. Flightdeck's kube client returns an empty Site object when CRD doesn't exist (instead of erroring)
4. Ready endpoint treats missing CRDs as non-fatal

title: feat: add passthrough config mechanism for Connect, Package Manager, and Workbench
description:
## Summary

- Adds escape-hatch passthrough fields to all three product configs (Connect, Package Manager, Workbench) so users can set arbitrary config values without waiting for operator releases
- Connect & PM: `additionalConfig` string, raw content appended after the generated config
- Workbench: `additionalConfigs` map with config file name keys, raw content appended per file
- Site CRD propagation for all three products
- Fixes pre-existing typo: `WorkbenchLauncherKubnernetesResourcesConfigSection` → `WorkbenchLauncherKubernetesResourcesConfigSection`

## Motivation

The operator currently defines ~25-33% of each product's config values as typed Go struct fields. Adding a new setting requires modifying 4+ files, running codegen, and releasing a new operator version. This passthrough mechanism lets users set any config value immediately.

## Design

### Connect & Package Manager (gcfg format)
```yaml
config:
  Server:
    Address: "typed-value.com"
  additionalConfig: |
    [Server]
    DataDir = /custom/path
    [NewSection]
    NewKey = any-value
```
- Raw gcfg content appended after the generated config
- gcfg parsing naturally resolves conflicts: last occurrence wins for scalar values, list values are combined
- Consistent with how Workbench handles passthrough

### Workbench (multiple config files)
```yaml
config:
  additionalConfigs:
    "rserver.conf": |
      session-timeout-minutes=120
      custom-setting=value
    "rsession.conf": |
      r-cran-repos=https://custom.repo.com
  additionalSessionConfigs:
    "repos.conf": |
      CRAN=https://custom.cran.com
```
- Keys are config file names
- Content appended after generated config
- Per-file approach handles Workbench's multiple formats (INI, DCF, JSON, newline-delimited)

title: feat: adds pdbs to workbench sessions
description:
Adds Pod Disruption Budgets (PDBs) for Workbench session pods to prevent user sessions from being evicted during node drains or cluster maintenance.                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                   
**Problem**                                                                                                                          

Previously, only Workbench server pods had PDB protection. Session pods had no eviction protection. During node drains or cluster scaling, Kubernetes/Karpenter could terminate active user sessions without warning.
                                                                                                                                   
  **Solution**                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                   
  Creates a second PDB for each Workbench spec that targets session pods:                                                               
  - Name: \<site\>-workbench-sessions                                                                                                
  - Selector: launcher-instance-id: \<site\>-workbench                                  
  - Policy: maxUnavailable: 0 (no sessions can be evicted)                                                                         
                                                                                                                                   
  This ensures user sessions remain persistent and uninterruptible during cluster operations.

title: fix(helm): sync CRDs and fix helm-generate post-processing
description:
## Summary

- Sync Helm chart CRDs with base CRDs to include recent API changes (`sessionTolerations`, `flightdeck.enabled`)
- Add Makefile post-processing to fix kubebuilder-generated files after `helm-generate`
- Remove unused `resourcePolicy.keep` feature from all templates
- Delete `config/rbac/auth_proxy_service.yaml` to prevent duplicate service creation

## Technical Context

### Why CRDs were out of sync

The base CRDs in `config/crd/bases/` are generated from `api/*_types.go` via `make manifests`. The Helm chart CRDs in `dist/chart/templates/crd/` are generated from the base CRDs via `make helm-generate`. However, `helm-generate` was only run once when Helm charts were first migrated, causing drift as new API fields were added.

**Solution:** Regenerated Helm CRDs from base CRDs. Going forward, developers should run `make helm-generate` after API changes.

### Why Makefile post-processing is needed

The kubebuilder helm plugin generates `certificate.yaml` and `metrics-service.yaml` from **internal Go templates** (not from `config/`). These templates hardcode the metrics service name as `team-operator-controller-manager-metrics-service`.

Since we template the `serviceAccountName` via Helm values, the service name should be `{{ .Values.controllerManager.serviceAccountName }}-metrics-service`. The sed commands in the Makefile patch these generated files to use the templated value.

**There is no source file to modify** - the templates live inside the kubebuilder binary itself.

### Why resourcePolicy.keep was removed

This Helm annotation (`helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`) prevents resources from being deleted on uninstall. For CRDs, we already have the dedicated `crd.keep` value. For other resources (RBAC, services, etc.), we want standard Helm lifecycle management - they should be cleaned up when the release is uninstalled.

### Why auth_proxy_service.yaml was deleted

The metrics service is already defined in `dist/chart/templates/metrics/metrics-service.yaml`. Having a source file in `config/rbac/auth_proxy_service.yaml` caused kubebuilder to generate a duplicate in `dist/chart/templates/rbac/auth_proxy_service.yaml`. Deleting the source file prevents this duplicate.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `helm template team-operator dist/chart` and verify no duplicate services
- [ ] Verify certificate dnsNames include the templated service name
- [ ] Deploy to test cluster and verify metrics endpoint works

title: feat(workbench): add init container for load balancer config
description:
## Summary

Adds an init container to Workbench deployments that creates the `/mnt/load-balancer/rstudio/load-balancer` file when load balancing is enabled. This file is required for RStudio Workbench to properly coordinate between multiple replicas.

## Problem

When running Workbench with multiple replicas (`LoadBalancingEnabled=1`), each pod needs to register itself with the load balancer by creating a configuration file containing:
- Its IP address (`www-host-name`)
- A flag to clean up on exit (`delete-node-on-exit`)

Previously, this file was not being created, which prevented proper load balancing across replicas.

## Solution

Following the pattern from the [RStudio Helm chart's prestart-workbench.bash](https://github.com/rstudio/helm/blob/main/charts/rstudio-workbench/prestart-workbench.bash), we add:

1. **Init container** (`load-balancer-init`) - A lightweight busybox container that runs before the main Workbench container to create the load-balancer config file with the pod's IP address

2. **EmptyDir volume** (`load-balancer-config`) - Shared between init and main containers, mounted at `/mnt/load-balancer`

3. **Conditional activation** - All of this is only enabled when `LoadBalancingEnabled == 1` in the Workbench spec

## Changes

- `internal/controller/core/workbench.go`:
  - Added `isLoadBalancingEnabled()` helper
  - Added `buildWorkbenchInitContainers()` to create the init container
  - Added `buildLoadBalancerVolumeMounts()` and `buildLoadBalancerVolumes()` for volume management
  - Integrated init containers, volume mounts, and volumes into the deployment spec

- `internal/controller/core/workbench_test.go`:
  - Added `TestWorkbenchLoadBalancingInitContainer` - verifies init container, volumes, and mounts are created when load balancing is enabled
  - Added `TestWorkbenchLoadBalancingDisabled` - verifies no init container or volumes when load balancing is disabled

## How to verify

1. Deploy a Workbench with `LoadBalancingEnabled: 1` in the spec
2. Check that the pod has an init container named `load-balancer-init`
3. Verify the file `/mnt/load-balancer/rstudio/load-balancer` exists in the main container
4. File should contain `delete-node-on-exit=1` and `www-host-name=<pod-ip>`

## Test plan

- [x] Code compiles (`go build ./...`)
- [x] Unit tests pass
- [x] Manually tested on ganso01-staging with 5 replicas
  - Deployed adhoc image `ghcr.io/posit-dev/team-operator:adhoc-feat-workbench-load-balancer-init-v1.3.2-6-g4ac14b9`
  - Verified load-balancer file created correctly in each pod:
    ```
    delete-node-on-exit=1
    www-host-name=<pod-ip>
    ```
  - All 5 Workbench replicas running successfully (2/2 Ready)
  - Load balancing distributed events working across replicas

title: feat: add local integration testing infrastructure (envtest + kind)
description:
## Summary

Implements #51: a two-tier local integration testing strategy so developers can validate operator behavior without deploying to staging clusters.

**Before:** the only way to test controller behavior against a real Kubernetes API was deploying to an internal staging cluster.
**After:** fast local alternatives that work offline, run in CI, and support an iterative dev loop.

---

## What This Adds

### Tier 1: Envtest (~5s, no cluster)

Tests CRD schema validation and API storage against a real embedded K8s API server — no kubelet, no containers, no Docker.

- Enabled the previously-skipped envtest suite in `suite_test.go`, fixing CRD paths and registering all required schemes (keycloak, traefik, secrets-store-csi-driver)
- 4 Ginkgo specs covering Site, Connect, Workbench, and PackageManager CRDs (`internal/controller/core/site_envtest_test.go`)

### Tier 2: Kind cluster (minutes, full stack)

Tests the full operator Helm deployment and Site CR reconciliation end-to-end against a real cluster.

- `hack/test-kind.sh` — deploys operator via Helm, creates a Site CR, verifies Connect and Workbench child CRs are reconciled, checks operator logs for panics, cleans up
- `make test-kind` runs `helm-generate` before deploying so the chart is always in sync with the current API

### Persistent Dev Loop

Instead of creating and destroying a cluster on every run, developers can keep a cluster alive across iterations:

```bash
make kind-setup    # create cluster + deploy operator (run once, or after code changes)
make kind-test     # run tests against the live cluster
make kind-teardown # clean up when done
```

`make kind-setup` is idempotent — running it after a code change rebuilds the image, reloads it into kind, and does a `helm upgrade`, so it doubles as the "reload" step.

### CI Integration

- Envtest runs on every PR
- Kind tests run on PRs that touch relevant paths (`api/**`, `internal/**`, `cmd/**`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, `go.mod/sum`, `dist/chart/**`, `hack/test-kind.sh`) via a `check-changes` job using `dorny/paths-filter`
- Kind tests also run on push to main, nightly, and manual dispatch

### Bug Fix

`cleanupLegacyHomeApp` was using a direct type assertion (`err.(*meta.NoKindMatchError)`) that misses wrapped errors, causing reconciliation to abort on any cluster without the secrets-store CSI driver (e.g. kind). Changed to `errors.As`.

### Documentation

- `README.md`: new Testing section surfacing both the one-shot and dev loop workflows as the primary recommended approach
- `docs/testing.md`: full reference — prerequisites, all targets, development loop, troubleshooting, best practices

---

## Test Plan

- [x] All existing unit tests continue to pass
- [x] `make go-test` exits cleanly
- [x] Kind tests pass end-to-end locally (`make test-kind`)
- [x] Dev loop tested: `kind-setup` → `kind-test` → code change → `kind-setup` → `kind-test` → `kind-teardown`
- [x] CI workflow triggers correctly on path-matched PRs

## Summary

Adds support for Workbench custom OAuth integrations by implementing the `oauth-clients.conf` configuration file format as documented at https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/integration/custom-oauth.html.

This feature allows users to configure multiple OAuth integrations (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, etc.) for their Workbench instances, enabling data access from external APIs.

## Backwards Compatibility

✅ **This change is fully backwards compatible:**

- The `OAuthClients` field is optional - existing Workbench CRs without it continue to work unchanged
- Nil `OAuthClients` is handled as a no-op (verified by unit test)
- Existing Databricks configurations are unaffected (verified by unit test)
- No changes to existing API fields or behavior
- Feature is additive only - no breaking changes

## Implementation Details

- **Added `WorkbenchOAuthClientConfig` struct** with fields for name, client-id, client-secret, authorization-url, token-url, token-endpoint-auth-method, and scopes
- **Added `OAuthClients` map field** to `WorkbenchSecretIniConfig` - map keys become INI section headers
- **Added `FetchAndSetOAuthClientSecrets()` method** to fetch secrets from vault (K8s Secrets or AWS Secrets Manager)
- **Integrated secret fetching** into `ReconcileWorkbench()` reconciliation loop (non-fatal errors)
- **Added OAuth secrets** to AWS SecretProviderClass for secret mounting
- **Fixed bug** in `GenerateConfigMap()` where slices in map-based configs were not converted to comma-separated strings
- **Added comprehensive API documentation** with kubebuilder validation markers
- **Added required field validation** (client-id, authorization-url, token-url)

## Test Coverage

title: fix: resolve Flightdeck reconciliation loop and improve owner references
description:
## Summary

- Fixes #6 (Flightdeck Reconciliation Loop)
- Addresses #11 (SetControllerReference for owner references)

This PR replaces the custom `BasicCreateOrUpdate` function with controller-runtime's `controllerutil.CreateOrUpdate` pattern, which:

1. **Only updates when objects actually change** - Prevents unnecessary reconciliation loops
2. **Uses `SetControllerReference`** - Properly sets `Controller=true` and `BlockOwnerDeletion=true` on owner references

### Root Cause (Issue #6)

The FlightdeckReconciler was the only controller using `.Owns()` to watch child resources. Combined with `BasicCreateOrUpdate` which unconditionally called `r.Update()` on every reconciliation, this created an infinite loop:

```
Reconcile → Update child → Watch fires → Reconcile → Update child → ...
```

### Solution

New `CreateOrUpdateResource` helper that wraps `controllerutil.CreateOrUpdate`:
- Uses a `MutateFn` pattern - only updates if the mutation actually changes the object
- Automatically sets controller references via `SetControllerReference`
- Maintains the existing managed-by label validation for security

### Changes

| Commit | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `feat: add CreateOrUpdateResource helper` | New function in `kubernetes_crudding.go` |
| `fix: migrate FlightdeckReconciler` | Fixes the reconciliation loop (6 call sites) |
| `refactor: update shared helpers` | `rbac.go`, `traefik.go`, `disruption_budget.go` |
| `refactor: migrate site controllers` | 10 files |
| `refactor: migrate product controllers` | `workbench`, `connect`, `package_manager`, `chronicle` |
| `chore: mark BasicCreateOrUpdate as deprecated` | Deprecation notice |

### What's Not Changed

- `BasicCreateNoUpdate` - For PersistentVolumes (create-only, no loop issue)
- `PvcCreateOrUpdate` - Has special PVC storage comparison logic
- Test files - Still use `BasicCreateOrUpdate` for test setup
